newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian steelmaker Clabecq may resume work.
newsitem.headline: Belgian steelmaker Clabecq may resume work.

text.p: Belgian steelmaker Forges de Clabecq may re-start work within a month after the Belgian authorities and a group of banks agreed a plan to keep the company momentarily afloat while searching for a potential buyer.
"The important thing is that the company is ready to resume work within a month, so that if we find a buyer we can re-start immediately," liquidator Alain Zenner told Belgian radio RTBF on Sunday.
Clabecq was declared bankrupt in January after the government of the Belgian Wallon region, a key shareholder, pulled the plug on the loss-making firm.
But on Friday the region and the creditor banks agreed to go-ahead with an interim plan allowing the company to survive another three months.

Under the terms of the plan, the region will inject 150 million Belgian francs into Clabecq and Belgian banks Generale de Banque and Banque Bruxelles Lambert will waive guarantees totalling respectively 135 millions and 55 millions, Belgian media said.
The plan, which was rejected by the banks only last week, was reluctanly backed by the firm's workers at a meeting on Saturday.
But the long-term future of the steelmaker continues to hinge on a search for a takeover candidate.

Some 2,000 families in the towns of Tubize and Rebecq, in an area which already resembles a post-industrial era wasteland, depend on Clabecq for work and unionists have fanatically been defending the jobs, even resorting to physical violence in some instances.

Clabecq's death sentence was signed in December when the European Commission rejected a regional aid plan, brandishing it as inadmissible state aid for a firm without a future in an industry suffering from overcapacity.
Saddled with high costs, poor margins and low-quality products, Clabecq had struggled to survive in a cyclical industry marked by overcapacity and cheap imports from eastern Europe.

Other Belgian steel firms have so far been cool on the idea of a cooperation or merger with Clabecq, either because they are not interested in its products -- mainly heavy plate -- or because they have already found another partner.
Unlisted Usines Gustave Boel is en route for a joint venture with Hoogovens of the Netherlands, which says, UGB complements its own business.
Belgium's largest steelmaker Cockerill Sambre has ruled out partnerships with UGB or Clabecq.
